memory

In forest memories 1-48, many images are gathered under one title. In the Moment memory, photographs are imagined as continually in motion. What becomes different each time an image is revisited, selected or set alongside another? A photograph can settle a detail in a remembered scene and reopen the question of what the scene meant. The Library’s work on reconstructive memory asks what happens between one recollection of an event and the next. Forest memories 1-48 · memory · Reconstruction: A Concept of Memory

Reading note. Jung and alchemy. The Library’s Jung’s Alchemy × Memory explores recollection through images of dissolving and recombining. When an image from forest memories 1-48 brings a scene to mind, what is altered in the recollection? What does the language of alchemy let us describe about that alteration? Jung’s Alchemy × Memory in the Library
